angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 154,445 km at 35.23 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 28.3823 +/- 0.0216 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 35.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.222 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract): 154,445 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.19 +/- 0.004 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3099 +/- 51 K from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7166.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.024, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7166 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.5+/-0.5, from Barkaoui et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7166 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.2 dex, from Barkaoui et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7166 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.3869, from Barkaoui et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7166 (pscomppars): age 4 Gyr, from Barkaoui et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2637B/abstract)
